guidance.opening:
It is autumn of 1920, and you are in a landlord’s office in Boston. You are the person he asked to come in about a house that will not stay rented. The last family, the Costas, left for an asylum, and you are here because he wants to talk that over before anything else.

Howard Crane leans on the desk. “Place is empty again. Nobody will take it. I need someone who can look into why the last tenants ran and whether the house is even livable, then tell me straight. Sit down; we can get to the rest after I know who you are.”

He taps a pencil against a blotter. “So—who are you, and what do you do for a living? Rough answer’s fine.”
guidance.advice: 1920s Boston identity meeting only. Occupations must use listed names: Journalist, Private Investigator, Lawyer, Librarian, Police Detective, Police Officer, Professor, Antiquarian, Author, Doctor of Medicine, Parapsychologist, Clergy, Dilettante, Engineer, Criminal, and the rest of the packet list as they fit. Useful public skills: Library Use, Law, History, Fast Talk, Spot Hidden, Listen, Persuade, Credit Rating; English is assumed; Latin or Italian can be optional flavor, not required. Era kit: notebook, press card, cheap suit, medical bag, flashlight—ordinary belongings, nothing from the house. Public involvement: answered a landlord’s call about a property that will not re-let after the last tenants went to an asylum; daily pay and keys are not granted in this meeting. Optional ties (not facts): a cousin who rented nearby, a paper that ran a rumor, a clinic contact. Do not invent numbers, force a job, or reveal Crowe, chapel, sanitarium details, keys, cash, or a signed hire. Setup tool writes the card after a rough name and living.
guidance.handoff: The visitor has sat with landlord Howard Crane in his Boston office, autumn 1920. He has stated the public problem—a house that will not stay rented after the last tenants left for an asylum—and asked who the visitor is and what they do. No commission accepted, no keys, cash, address, or items given. Continue from that same office once identity is settled; research sites and the house remain ahead.
